title: The Roman Family
objective: After this level you can explain the power of the paterfamilias and how Roman families were organized.
summary: The paterfamilias held legal power over his descendants, even adults. The familia included the whole household, enslaved people too.

cards.headline: In a Roman family, a grown man could still be under his father’s legal power.
The father’s power
cards.body: Every Roman family had a paterfamilias: its oldest living male. He held legal power over his children and grandchildren, even when they were adults. In early Roman law this power, patria potestas, in theory reached as far as life and death.

cards.headline: More than relatives
cards.body: The Roman familia meant the whole household, including the enslaved people who lived and worked in it. Noble families also honored their dead: they kept wax masks of their ancestors and carried them in funeral processions.

cards.context: A Roman man’s name, like Gaius Julius Caesar, joined a personal name, a clan name and a family branch name.
